newsitem.title: GERMANY: Amnesty urges Germany to stop Afghan deportations.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty urges Germany to stop Afghan deportations.

text.p: The human rights group Amnesty International appealed to Germany on Wednesday to suspend deportations of Afghan asylum-seekers now that the Taleban radical militia has taken power in their homeland.
The militia, which captured the capital of Kabul last week, has executed a former president, banned women from workplaces and imposed other strict Islamic strictures on Afghan society.

"With the deterioration in the human rights situation, it is vital to institute general protection from deportation," Amnesty said in its appeal to Interior Minister Manfred Kanther and his counterparts in Germany's 16 regional states.
A spokeswoman for the group said there were around 5,800 Afghan asylum-seekers in Germany threatened with deportation.
The Taleban, which began as a movement of theology students and now controls three quarters of the country, has also decreed death by stoning for adultery and amputation of hands for theft.
